messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Realtime latency regression detected for prod-us-east-1 /api/generate (p99 > 2.5s for 3 windows). Rule: latency.realtime.p99 > 2.5s. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/latency/prod-us-east-1

incident-bot: Alert details:
```
query: fastapi.response_time.p99{env:prod,region:us-east-1,route:/api/generate} > 2.5s over 3m
window: 1m
count: 3
```

oncall: @alex (oncall-sre) pager routed

alex: I'm on it, joining now. Paging @maria and @kevin for runtime + model hints.

maria: seeing correlated spike on streaming endpoints (`/v1/stream`) too. p95 up from ~220ms -> ~1.1s, p99 around 2.8s. Logs show increased `kv_cache_miss` events.

kevin: confirmed — kernel traces from serving runtime show longer kernel times on sequence lengths > 1024. Could be a bad rollout of a quantized variant last night? ops-bot, any deploys in the last 12h?

ops-bot: deploy notice: `deploy/2026-03-14T22:14:00` -> prod-us-east-1 -> model-variant:v2q finished at 2026-03-14T22:14:27 by ci/cd. No rollbacks on file.

sam: quick triage checklist:
- Grafana: latency spike started ~22:20 UTC, correlation with increased KV misses and inference queue length.
- Traces: tail spans show 1) backend wait for KV cache rebuild, 2) worker desched during GC.
- Alerts: p95+p99 both triggered, but error rate unchanged. Looks like tail latency/regression, not errors.

alex: ok, mitigation proposals (fast):
1) Route latency-sensitive traffic to fallback model (model-variant:v2fp) using smart routing policy for the next 30m.
2) Temporarily increase dedicated pool by +20% (scale up) in us-east-1.
3) Disable the new quantized runtime path for v2q if it's the suspect.
4) Reduce batching windows to cut tail latency (trade higher token cost).
Please call out if any are risky for accuracy-sensitive customers.

maria: routing to fallback sounds good. v2fp has slightly higher cost but stable. I'm planning to flip the routing policy now. Doing `rdwctl routing set --route /api/generate --fallback model:v2fp --duration 30m --reason "p99 regression"`

kevin: I'm rolling a fast disable of the quant path on the serving fleet (canary then global) — will watch kernel times. If we hit regressions on canary, rollback to prior config. Command run:
```
servectl config set --param enable_quant_kpath=false --env prod --region us-east-1 --canary 5%
```

sam: also lowering batch window from 20ms -> 8ms on the latency-sensitive route. Executing change. Expect immediate reduction in p99 but higher throughput cost.

alex: good. Maria — can you confirm which tenants hit >1s p95? we need customer impact.

maria: quick query shows top impacted tenants: `tenant-alpha`, `tenant-beta`, `tenant-legacy-3`. Roughly 12% of active traffic experiencing >1s p95 during spike. No 5xx spike. Posting short impact note to #customer-impact channel.

lina: watching traces — after starting routing change (t+35s) I can see p99 drop from 2.8s -> ~1.1s on fallback traffic. Overall cluster p99 dropping slowly as canary scales.

ops-bot: Autoscaler action: increased dedicated-pool-us-east-1 from 75 -> 90 replicas (20% up).

kevin: canary shows kernel times back to baseline, quant path appears to be the culprit. I'm promoting the disable to 100% in prod-us-east-1.

alex: rolling disable to 100%. After rollout, re-evaluate for 15m then decide on permanent fix or revert with a patched quant kernel.

sam: p95 now ~260ms, p99 ~780ms (was 2.8s) — continuing to monitor.

maria: created incident tracker doc: https://docs.redwood.example/incidents/1829990000 (summary + timeline + mitigation steps + customer impact). Adding list of affected tenants + mitigation notes.

alex: handoff plan for the next shift: - Owner: alex (oncall-sre) till 23:30 UTC - Follow-ups: kevin investigate quant kernel regression and prepare patch; maria verify cache warming strategy and KV cache config; sam verify cost impact of reduced batching and autoscale delta.

alex: recording short summary for post-incident: p99 regression caused by quantized kernel path increasing kernel microsecond times for long sequences -> KV cache pressure -> tail latency spike. Mitigations: fallback routing, disable quant path, scale up dedicated pool, reduce batching. Customer impact: ~12% traffic saw elevated p95, no increase in errors.

incident-bot: Incident acknowledged and logged: INC-2026-0314-1829990000. Pager unlatched.

alex: thanks everyone. I'll keep this thread updated if anything changes; otherwise will file full postmortem template in 24h. :thumbsup:
